memos.headline: AAPL, GOOGL, and CAT Lead on Trend and Relative Strength; PG and MSFT Lag Badly
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe: AAPL (+22.2% vs 200d, RSI 59), GOOGL (+56.4% vs 200d, RSI 70, 12w rel strength +29.4%), and CAT (at 52w high, +45.8% vs 200d, 12w rel strength +35.6%) are in powerful uptrends with strong relative strength versus SPY. On the other side, PG is in a confirmed downtrend—RSI 36.7, -9.5% below its 200d mean, -18.6% drawdown, and 12w rel strength of -13.8%—while MSFT sits below its 50d mean with negative 4w and 12w relative strength. NVDA and AMZN are in no-man's-land: both below their 50d means with weakening relative strength but still above their 200d means, so I'm neutral until they resolve. I'd ride the momentum in AAPL and CAT but note that GOOGL and CAT are both touching RSI 70, so I'd tighten stops—a close below the 50d mean (~$275 for GOOGL, ~$540 for CAT) would change my view.

views.note: Strong uptrend, +5% above 50d, only -2.6% from highs, RSI 59 not yet overbought; would reassess on a close below ~265 (50d area).
Parabolic move with +90% 26w return and dominant relative strength, but RSI 70.1 and +17% above 50d mean warn of near-term pullback risk; a close below ~275 (50d area) would flip me neutral.
Sitting at its 52w high with +75% 26w return and massive relative strength; RSI 70 and extreme extension above 200d (+45.8%) mean I'd trail a tight stop near ~540.
Clear downtrend: -9.5% below 200d, RSI 36.7, -18.6% drawdown, and persistent negative relative strength; no reason to step in until price reclaims its 200d mean (~$158).
Below 50d mean, negative 4w and 12w relative strength vs SPY, RSI 42; would need a reclaim of ~$507 (50d area) to reconsider.
Mixed signals: well above 200d but below 50d, RSI 47.6, and 4w relative strength -5.3%; waiting for a decisive break above ~$187 (50d) or below ~$155 (200d).
Flat near 50d mean but 4w relative strength of -7.9% is concerning; need a reclaim of $243 (recent highs) to get constructive.
Healthy uptrend above both moving averages and near highs, but 4w and 12w relative strength are slightly negative; inline with SPY, not a standout.
Despite a recent 4w bounce of +2.9%, the -45.8% drawdown from highs and -8.6% below 200d mean signal a broken chart; would need sustained closes above ~$362 (200d area) to reconsider.
Quiet and orderly near highs with RSI 51 and low volatility, but zero relative strength vs SPY over 4w and 12w; no edge either way.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Show Durable Earnings Power; UNH Margin Collapse and XOM Revenue Decline Warrant Caution
memos.body: I see the strongest fundamental setups in NVDA and GOOGL this quarter. NVDA posted $57.01B in quarterly revenue (+62.5% YoY) with a staggering 56.0% net margin and only $8.47B in total debt—this is the cleanest earnings power story in the universe. GOOGL delivered $102.35B in revenue (+15.9% YoY) at a 34.2% net margin with minimal leverage ($14.79B debt), while MSFT's 18.4% revenue growth and 35.7% net margin remain best-in-class among scaled software names. On the other side, UNH's net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to just $2.35B on a 2.1% net margin despite 12.2% revenue growth, signaling severe cost or reserve pressures that I cannot underwrite, and XOM's revenue fell 5.2% with net income down 12.3%—a commodity earnings compression I want to avoid. The line items that would change my view: UNH's medical loss ratio stabilizing and XOM's upstream realizations recovering.

views.note: 62.5% YoY revenue growth, 56.0% net margin, and only $8.47B total debt represent the most compelling earnings power profile in the universe.
15.9% revenue growth with a 34.2% net margin and low $14.79B debt load shows durable, high-quality earnings expansion.
18.4% YoY revenue growth to $77.67B and a 35.7% net margin on moderate $43.21B debt make this a core compounder, though net income growth of 12.5% lagged revenue.
Revenue of $180.17B (+13.4% YoY) with net income up 38.2% to $21.19B shows margin leverage, but 11.8% net margin still leaves room for execution risk.
Revenue grew 7.9% and net income surged 86.4% (likely off a depressed base), but $90.68B in total debt and single-digit top-line growth limit upside conviction.
Solid 31.0% net margin and 11.6% net income growth, but $427.2B total debt and macro sensitivity keep me at neutral.
Steady 21.2% net margin and 20% net income growth are reassuring, but only 3.0% revenue growth limits the earnings growth runway.
Revenue grew 9.5% but net income fell 6.7%, indicating margin compression that needs to reverse before I can get constructive.
Net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to $2.35B on a 2.1% net margin despite 12.2% revenue growth—severe margin deterioration I cannot underwrite until the medical loss ratio stabilizes.
Revenue declined 5.2% and net income fell 12.3% to $7.55B with an 8.8% net margin, reflecting commodity-driven earnings compression.

memos.headline: Fed in Easing Mode but Sticky 3% CPI and Rising Unemployment Signal a Cautious Late-Cycle Regime
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing cycle — the upper bound has dropped 75bp over the past year to 4.00% and 50bp in just the last three months, with the effective rate at 3.88%. However, CPI is running at 3.0% YoY (September print), which is still well above target, and the unemployment rate has risen 30bp over three months to 4.40%, suggesting the labor market is softening meaningfully. The 10y-2y spread has normalized sharply (+53bp YoY to +0.59pp), confirming the curve un-inversion that typically accompanies late-cycle slowdowns. I have moderate conviction that this easing-into-softening regime favors duration-sensitive quality growth and defensive staples over cyclicals and energy; a December CPI print above 3.2% or a payrolls miss pushing unemployment toward 4.6% would shift my call toward outright recession positioning.

views.note: High-quality duration asset benefits from continued rate cuts and defensive recurring-revenue profile in a softening economy.
Duration tailwind from easing cycle supports premium growth multiples, though consumer softening from rising unemployment is a modest headwind.
Defensive staple with pricing power should outperform as unemployment rises and the economy slows; lower rates reduce discount on stable cash flows.
Positive curve steepening (+53bp YoY in 10y-2y) helps NIM, but rising unemployment and further rate cuts compress short-end earnings — offsetting forces.
Classic cyclical facing headwinds from a softening labor market and still-elevated inflation squeezing real activity; not the regime for capex plays.
Late-cycle slowdown typically pressures commodity demand; rising unemployment and easing policy point to weaker energy pricing ahead.
Secular growth with high duration sensitivity benefits from falling rates, though elevated CPI keeps a floor under discount rates — moderate conviction.
Easing cycle supports growth multiples and consumer spending resilience for now, but watch unemployment closely for downside risk to retail segment.
Benefits from rate cuts like other growth names but ad revenue cyclicality introduces risk if unemployment continues to climb.
Defensive healthcare name is relatively rate-insensitive; macro regime neither strongly favors nor disfavors at current levels.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: AMZN and CAT Stand Out While MSFT and NVDA Face Negative Tone Drift
memos.body: I reviewed the earnings-season price reactions and subsequent 8-K filing cadence across the universe to gauge where sentiment momentum is building or fading. AMZN (+9.6%) and CAT (+11.6%) posted the strongest post-earnings pops, signaling decisively positive narrative shifts that likely attracted incremental coverage and positioning—though five weeks later some of that enthusiasm may be priced. MSFT (-2.9%) and NVDA (-3.2%) both sold off on results, and with no subsequent positive catalysts in their filing streams, the negative tone appears sticky and not yet fully absorbed. AAPL (-0.4%), PG (+0.2%), XOM (-0.3%), and UNH (+0.5%) all had muted reactions, suggesting consensus was already well-calibrated; UNH's string of governance-related filings (bylaw amendments, officer changes) adds a layer of uncertainty that could weigh on tone going forward. I have highest conviction on the AMZN/CAT positive divergence and the MSFT/NVDA negative drift, while the rest of the universe looks sentiment-neutral.

views.note: A +9.6% earnings pop and a follow-on 8-K suggest sustained positive narrative, though some of the move is likely priced after five weeks.
The +11.6% earnings reaction was the largest in the universe, indicating a genuine sentiment inflection for an industrial name that had been under pressure.
A -2.9% post-earnings drop with no subsequent positive filings suggests negative tone is persisting and may not yet be fully discounted.
The -3.2% sell-off on the most recent earnings (Nov 19) is fresh and negative sentiment has had little time to wash out.
A modest +2.5% earnings reaction and a routine follow-on 8-K leave sentiment balanced with no clear directional edge.
Flat earnings reaction (+0.5%) is overshadowed by a cluster of governance filings (bylaw changes, officer departures) that inject uncertainty without a clear negative catalyst.
A near-flat -0.4% earnings reaction signals consensus was already well-set; no subsequent filings shift the tone.
Muted +0.2% earnings reaction and a high volume of routine filings suggest stable but uninspiring sentiment.
A -0.3% earnings reaction and subsequent governance/other filings point to flat sentiment with no narrative shift.
The -1.9% earnings dip was modest and occurred early in the cycle (Oct 14); subsequent filings are routine, leaving tone roughly neutral now.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Surges 82% in One Month While Oil Slides—Divergent Signals Demand Caution on Export-Exposed Names
memos.body: I am flagging a stark divergence: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has spiked to 520 (+82% m/m, +34% 3m), the highest reading in recent memory, yet VIX has actually fallen 17% over the past month to 15.78 and HY spreads tightened 25bp. This tells me markets are pricing benign credit conditions even as policy risk—likely driven by tariff rhetoric, export-control escalation, and energy-security debates—is structurally elevated. WTI at $59.82 (-6.3% 3m) suggests either demand weakness or an expectation of looser OPEC+ discipline, which is a headwind for energy but a tailwind for input-cost-sensitive industrials and consumer staples. I have moderate conviction that semiconductor and cloud names with China revenue exposure (NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL) face asymmetric downside if the policy uncertainty translates into concrete export controls, while domestically oriented defensives (PG, UNH) and financials (JPM) are better positioned. A reversal in my view would require the EPU index to fall below 400 or a clear de-escalation in US-China tech restrictions.

views.note: Elevated policy uncertainty at 520 and ongoing export-control risk to China make NVDA the most exposed name in the universe; any new chip-restriction rule would be a structural headwind.
Cloud capex and AI ambitions carry indirect China-supply-chain risk, but diversified revenue and recent Reg FD disclosure suggest manageable near-term exposure.
WTI at $59.82 and falling 6.3% over three months pressures upstream margins; multiple recent 8-Ks suggest active capital-allocation moves, but weak oil caps upside absent a geopolitical supply shock.
Domestically oriented consumer staple benefits from lower oil-linked input costs and is insulated from export-control risk; four 8-K filings in six weeks suggest proactive investor communication.
Steepening yield curve (+7bp m/m to 0.59pp) and tight HY spreads at 2.88% support bank earnings; domestic focus limits direct geopolitical exposure.
Lower oil prices reduce mining/energy capex demand, but policy uncertainty could cut either way—infrastructure spending bills would be a positive catalyst, tariff escalation a negative one.
